title: Getting started
markdown:
## **Register an account**

Everyone who uses the platform should register their own account. Recommended registration practices:
- **Username:** Use an English name, the pinyin of your name, an employee ID, or a phone number. Usernames must be globally unique.
- **Nickname:** Use the name your colleagues normally call you, such as your real name, a familiar nickname, or an English name. This makes it easier to identify the right person when managing permissions or collaborating.
- **Email:** Use your internal company email address.

## **Create or join a Workspace**

### **Onboard a new project**

To onboard a project, create a new Workspace. Each project is isolated in its own Workspace. Here, a project means an independent system, such as a corporate website, supply chain management system, or visitor management system. One project can contain any number of frontend and backend Git repositories.

### **Join an existing project**

If someone on your team has already created the Workspace, you can join it in either of two ways:
1. Switch to “All Workspaces” on the Workspace list page, find the Workspace, and select “Request access”. A Workspace administrator approves the request in “Member management”.
2. Ask a Workspace administrator (the creator or a member with administrator access) to search for your nickname or login name in “Member management” and add you.

## **Use the platform**

### **Connect an Agent to the platform**

Open “Profile settings” at the top right, select “MCP tokens”, and create an MCP token. Configure this MCP connection in Qoder/Qoder CN. You can then use Qoder/Qoder CN to operate the platform: create Work items, analyze Delivery errors, or configure Squads, Agents, SDLC workflows, repositories, and Executors. AutoWonder is AI Native; we recommend using an Agent for complex and repetitive operations.

![MCP client configuration](/help/assets/02-en-US.png "")

After configuring MCP, ask your Agent to “Use AutoWonder MCP to operate the ‘XXX’ Workspace”. We recommend installing the `auto-wonder.zip` Skill in your Agent tool. For later operations on AutoWonder, enter `/auto-wonder` in the Agent.

[auto-wonder.zip](/help/assets/auto-wonder.zip)

The Skill content is shown below. It instructs your Agent to use the AutoWonder platform MCP to perform operations.
```markdown
---
name: auto-wonder
description: Use when the user invokes auto-wonder or asks to perform an operation through the AutoWonder platform.
---

# AutoWonder

Use the AutoWonder platform MCP to perform operations.

```

Example: ask `/auto-wonder` to analyze whether the Agents, their SDLC definitions, repository configuration, repository relationships, and Agent repository bindings in the Standard Automated Delivery Squad of the “XXX” Workspace are complete. Ask whether the Squad can deliver Work items automatically, which stages hand off automatically, and which need human intervention.
```markdown
/auto-wonder Analyze whether the Agents, their SDLC definitions, repository configuration, repository relationships, and Agent repository bindings in the Standard Automated Delivery Squad of the "XXX" Workspace are complete. Can the entire Squad deliver Work items automatically? Which stages hand off automatically, and which require human intervention?
```

**Project administrators:** If you administer a project Workspace and are responsible for onboarding the project, configure its Squads, Agents, SDLC workflows, repositories, and repository relationships for the actual project. This defines the AI automated Delivery pipeline and is a critical step best performed by someone who knows the project well. Continue to optimize, iterate on, and maintain the configuration to improve Delivery efficiency and quality and reduce token consumption. See the “Project onboarding” chapter for configuration instructions.

**Project team members:** If you work on development or testing and are responsible for Delivery, focus on the “Work items”, “Scheduled tasks”, and “Execution records” modules in the Delivery section to submit, clarify, and deliver requirements.

title: Project onboarding
markdown:
## **Setup steps**

### Step 1: Create a project Workspace

Create a new Workspace for the project.

### Step 2: Get the source and initialize templates

#### Get the project source

Clone the AutoWonder source locally using the following commands. Git sparse checkout downloads only the AutoWonder project source. If `git clone` is unavailable, download the source from Git instead: [https://github.com/aliyun/alibabacloud-landing-zone](https://github.com/aliyun/alibabacloud-landing-zone).

```markdown
git clone --filter=blob:none --no-checkout \
https://github.com/aliyun/alibabacloud-landing-zone.git

cd alibabacloud-landing-zone

git sparse-checkout init --no-cone

git sparse-checkout set /ai-sdlc/auto-wonder/

git checkout master
```

#### Set the Agent working directory

Create a session in Qoder/Qoder CN and set its working directory to `alibabacloud-landing-zone/ai-sdlc/auto-wonder`. This lets Qoder/Qoder CN discover the template initialization Skill in the AutoWonder source.

#### Initialize Workspace templates

Use the prompt below to initialize templates. The `initialize-autowonder-harness` Skill in the AutoWonder source imports templates containing Squads, Agents, and SDLC workflows into your Workspace. Templates make initial onboarding easier; once familiar with the platform, you can configure a project entirely yourself. A Flash model is sufficient; the Skill is expected to take about 20 minutes. Prerequisite: **the Agent must already be connected to AutoWonder through MCP**.

The example asks the Skill to initialize all templates in the “XXX” Workspace.
```markdown
/initialize-autowonder-harness Initialize all templates in the "XXX" Workspace.
```

**Example names:** The examples below use Quick Delivery Squad, Standard Automated Delivery Squad, Requirements Clarification, Quick Full-Stack Developer, Quick Deployment Engineer, and Project Manager. When working with your own configuration, refer to the actual Squad and Agent names in your Workspace.

### Step 3: Adapt templates to your project

#### Analyze template variables

After initialization, enter the following prompt in the same session. It asks the Agent to use AutoWonder MCP for the “XXX” Workspace and identify the `{{}}` variables in the Agents and SDLC definitions of “Quick Delivery Squad”. The initialized configuration is still the default template and needs project-specific values.

```markdown
For the rest of this session, use AutoWonder MCP to operate the "XXX" Workspace on the AutoWonder platform:
- Identify the variables in the Agents and their SDLC definitions in the Quick Delivery Squad. The Squad still uses the default initialized templates with variables in {{}} format. I need to update this configuration for my project.
```

#### Update the template configuration

Replace the identified variables with your project's actual information. Describe the project to the Agent and ask it to analyze and update the template configuration. The example covers:

- **Deployment:** If using Jenkins, explain that deployment triggering is packaged as a Skill uploaded to the Workspace, give its name “XXX”, and provide `ProjectID` and `JobID`. Ask the Agent to trigger deployment with that Skill. For local testing and deployment, select an unused random port between 18000 and 19000 to avoid conflicts between branches. Check whether the port is occupied before deployment and choose another in that range if necessary.
- **Database:** Provide the database version (MySQL 8.0 in the example), username `dev_user`, password `xxx`, and connection address and port `xxx`.
- **Branch merging before deployment:** If required, ask the Agent to merge the development branch into `dev` before deployment. If CICD receives branch information and merges it in the deployment pipeline, remove the branch-merging variables and explain that arrangement. Configure other cases according to the actual required stage and logic.

```markdown
# Update deployment information
For example, if your deployment environment uses Jenkins:
- My deployment environment is Jenkins. I have packaged its deployment trigger as a Skill and uploaded it to the Workspace. The Skill is named "XXX". Use this Skill to trigger deployment, with ProjectID set to XXX and JobID set to XXX.
If your project tests require a local startup, you can say:
My project is tested and validated locally, and deployment means starting it locally. To avoid port conflicts when multiple branches are deployed locally, randomly select a port between 18000 and 19000. Before deployment, check whether the selected port is occupied; if it is, choose another port in the same range.

# Update database information
My database is MySQL 8.0. The username is dev_user, the password is xxx, and the connection address and port are xxx.

# Merge branches before deployment
If you need to merge into dev before deployment, say: Merge the current development branch into dev before deployment.
If you pass branch information to the deployment pipeline and CICD merges it automatically, say: Remove the branch-merging variables. My deployment passes the current development branch to the CICD pipeline, which performs the merge.
For other arrangements, configure the branch-merging stage and logic according to your actual requirements.

```

Give this information to the Agent so it can combine the variable analysis and actual project details to update the configuration.

### Step 4: Configure repositories and MCP

#### Configure repositories and their relationships

Describe all project repositories and their relationships to the Agent so it can configure and associate them. The sample prompt asks it to configure the repositories and descriptions, set their relationships, bind every repository to every Agent with `Write` permission, and automatically publish and approve the Agents afterward.

The sample uses four `https://gitlab.com/xxx.git` repositories with the `master` default branch: the backend repository contains Java backend business code; the frontend repository contains Vue client code; the API repository contains Java interface definitions; and the middleware repository contains Java database and Redis code. The frontend depends on the backend, which depends on the API and middleware repositories.

```markdown
Configure the following repository information and descriptions in my project Workspace, and configure the repository relationships provided below. Then bind all repositories to every Agent with Write permission, and automatically publish and approve the Agents.

Project repositories:
Backend repository: https://gitlab.com/xxx.git, default branch: master
Frontend repository: https://gitlab.com/xxx.git, default branch: master
API repository: https://gitlab.com/xxx.git, default branch: master
Middleware repository: https://gitlab.com/xxx.git, default branch: master

Repository descriptions:
The backend repository contains the project's Java server code. Develop all backend business code in this repository.
The frontend repository contains the project's Vue client code. Develop all frontend code in this repository.
The API repository contains all of the project's Java interface definitions. Develop all interface definitions in this repository.
The middleware repository contains all of the project's Java database and Redis operations. Develop all database and Redis code in this repository.

Repository relationships:
The frontend repository depends on the backend repository.
The backend repository depends on the API and middleware repositories.
```

This step defines the project's repositories, relationships, and development boundaries and associates them with Agents. Agents can then pull branches from the right repositories for development, testing, and deployment.

#### Configure MCP for Agents

Configure the AutoWonder platform MCP for Agents so each Agent can read platform information during execution. In “Personal settings”, create an MCP named “AutoWonder” and configure it in the current Workspace. Then ask the Agent to apply that MCP to all Agents. The prompt below asks it to configure the Workspace's “AutoWonder” MCP on every Agent and automatically publish and approve them afterward.

```markdown
Bind the "AutoWonder" MCP configured in my project Workspace to every Agent, then automatically publish and approve the Agents.
```





### Step 5: Validate the Delivery workflow

Before starting Delivery, ask the Agent to analyze whether the configuration is correct. The example asks it to examine the Agents, SDLC workflows, repositories, repository relationships, and Agent repository bindings in “Quick Delivery Squad”; determine whether automated Delivery can proceed; identify automatic stages and stages requiring human decisions; and provide the entire Delivery workflow as a Markdown flowchart. It also asks that `Soul.md` and `Agent.md` contain only shared Agent information, while information needed only by a specific SDLC step belongs in that step rather than all being placed in `Agent.md`.

```markdown
Fully analyze whether the Agents, SDLC workflows, repositories, repository relationships, and Agent repository bindings in the Quick Delivery Squad of the current Workspace are correct. Can the current configuration deliver a requirement automatically? Which stages run automatically, and which require human decisions? Provide the entire Delivery workflow as a Markdown flowchart.
Note: Configure only shared Agent information in Soul.md and Agent.md. Put information needed only by a specific SDLC step in that step's configuration, rather than putting all information in Agent.md.
```

Review the Agent's findings and decide whether further improvements are needed. The workflow configuration is central: its correctness directly determines whether Delivery completes as expected.

### Step 6: Prepare the runtime and register Executors

#### Install the CLI and plugins

On the machine where you will register Executors, download and install Qoder/QoderCN CLI and the SuperPowers plugin. You can use your own computer for initial trials; for stable operation, use a machine that can run continuously, such as a Linux server, desktop, or Mac mini. Get the CLI installation command from the Qoder website ([https://qoder.com/zh/cli](https://qoder.com/zh/cli)) or QoderCN website ([https://qoder.cn/cli](https://qoder.cn/cli)), install the CLI, and configure its environment variables. Alternatively, give the installation command to an Agent and ask it to install Qoder CLI and configure the environment variables, replacing `xxx` with the actual command.

```markdown
Install Qoder CLI using this command and configure its environment variables. Installation command: xxx
```

After installation, run `qoder` or `qodercn` in the terminal and sign in. Then ask the CLI to install SuperPowers. Clarification uses SuperPowers to clarify requirements and generate Agent-oriented Spec and Plan files. If you already use a plugin such as OpenSpec, you can install that instead, but also update the instructions in the Requirements Clarification Agent's `Agent.md`. We recommend SuperPowers based on practices used by many enterprises. The example asks for a user-level installation from the official plugin address `https://github.com/obra/superpowers`.
```markdown
Install the SuperPowers plugin at the user level. Official plugin URL: https://github.com/obra/superpowers
```

#### Register and start Executors

Ask your Agent to configure Executors for all Agents in “Quick Delivery Squad” and for the Requirements Clarification Agent. Adjust the prompt for Qoder or Qoder CN as appropriate. The example specifies Qoder CLI (or Qoder CN CLI), platform memory, the latest Qwen flagship model for Clarification (for example `Qwen3.8-Max`), the latest Qwen Flash model for other Agents (the original example spells it `Qwne3.8-Flash`), `Medium` reasoning effort, a `1M` context window, and Executor names formed from “NO1” plus the Agent name. It then asks for every Executor's startup command in an `autowonder-executor` script on the desktop supporting `start`, `stop`, and `status`.

```markdown
Configure Executors for every Agent in the Quick Delivery Squad and for the Requirements Clarification Agent:
- Select Qoder CLI as the client type. If you use Qoder CN, select Qoder CN CLI instead.
- Use platform memory.
- Use the latest Qwen flagship model for Requirements Clarification, such as Qwen3.8-Max. Use the latest Qwen Flash model for the other Agents, such as Qwne3.8-Flash.
- Select Medium reasoning effort.
- Select a 1M context window.
- Name each Executor using "NO1" plus the Agent name.

After configuring the Executors, retrieve all their startup commands and package them in a script named autowonder-executor on my desktop. The script must support start, stop, and status commands.
```

Run the generated script on your computer or server to register Executors, then check the “Executors” page to confirm they are online.



## First Work item Delivery

Configuration is now complete. Create a Work item to try Delivery. There are two steps:
- Clarification.
- Start the task.

### Step 1

Start Clarification. The Agent uses the requirement and latest code to clarify it with you. At the last step, it presents the proposed design for confirmation. After you confirm, it generates `spec.md` and `plan.md` and uploads them as Work item attachments. If the design needs changes, continue providing feedback until it meets your requirements, then confirm it.

**Note:** For Clarification, select **“Standard Automated Delivery Squad”**, which contains the Requirements Clarification Agent, then select the **“Requirements Clarification”** Agent and start.

![Clarification conversation](/help/assets/06-en-US.png "")



### Step 2

Return to the Work item and start Delivery with the “Quick Full-Stack Developer” Agent in “Quick Delivery Squad”. If you later configure other Delivery Squads, choose the appropriate Squad. In the Quick Delivery template, the full-stack development Agent automatically hands off to “Quick Deployment Engineer” for deployment after development and testing finish.



![Start Delivery](/help/assets/09-en-US.png "")

Your first project is now onboarded and its first Delivery has started. Subsequent users only need to create a Work item → clarify requirements → start Delivery.

In “Member management”, search by username to add teammates to this project Workspace and assign their permissions. There are three access levels:
- **Read only:** View project information without performing operations.
- **Read and write:** Create Work items, perform Clarification, and start Work items.
- **Administrator:** Manage project configuration, including Squads, Agents, SDLC workflows, repositories, and Executors.



Refer to “Best practices” and continue refining the AI automated Delivery pipeline to fit your project.

title: IM integration
markdown:
## **Configure the platform bot**

A platform administrator configures a bot for the chosen IM tool in “Platform configuration” on the Workspace list page. The bot needs permission to send messages and read contacts.





## **Set your Employee ID**

Every platform user should set their Employee ID in “Personal settings” so system notifications can reach them through the configured IM tool.



## **Configure a project bot**

Each project can configure a project-level bot for two-way communication. Add it to a group chat to discuss requirements and dispatch tasks related to the platform. For example, ask how many Work items were completed today or whether a Work item has already been submitted for a particular requirement.

The project group-chat bot is usually configured on the “Project Manager” Agent. This Agent does not carry out specific Delivery work. It views, coordinates, and analyzes platform information and invokes the appropriate Agents for concrete work and instructions. Refer to the “Project Manager” Agent definition in the templates for details.

![Project Manager bot configuration](/help/assets/14-en-US.png "")

title: Best practices
markdown:
## **Manage account permissions**
1. **Change the default `admin` account password promptly after the first login.**
2. After deployment, you can use the initialized `admin` account to configure the platform. For daily use, sign in with your own registered account so audit logs identify the operator. If you need to manage the platform, grant your personal account the platform administrator role instead of continuing to use the shared `admin` account.
3. Platform administrators can grant that role to others as needed in “Platform configuration”. We recommend giving platform administrator access to the person responsible for the platform.
4. Give project administrator access only to people who maintain the project configuration. Allowing everyone to modify configuration and register Executors can create confusion.

## **Executors**
1. For initial setup, register Executors on one computer, with one Executor per Agent. Avoid registering too many: Delivery tasks are automatically scheduled across available Executors according to load. During debugging and validation, tasks may otherwise be sent to another machine and stop if it shuts down or sleeps, making debugging harder.
2. After validation, run production Executors in an environment that can operate continuously, such as a Linux server or Mac mini. Windows is not recommended for long-term operation because problems such as garbled text can occur. If Windows is required, install WSL and register Executors in its Linux environment.
3. Install every project dependency in the Executor environment. For a Java project, for example, install JDK, Maven, and Git. Development, testing, and validation all run in that environment.

## **Qoder accounts**
1. A personal account is suitable for signing in to Qoder CLI during initial testing and validation. For stable long-term operation, apply for an account representing the team and allocate sufficient Credits for production Delivery. Delivery consumes the Credits of the Qoder account signed in on the Executor, rather than those of the person who submits the Work item.

## **Work item Delivery**
1. Submit requirements and bug fixes as Work items. Delivery runs around each Work item, the configured Agents, and their SDLC workflows.
2. For questions during Delivery, such as progress, error causes, or solutions, @mention the relevant Agent in the Work item's comments.

## **Optimize costs**
1. For non-urgent production requirements, schedule Delivery during off-peak hours, such as 10 p.m., to benefit from applicable off-peak discounts and reduce Credit consumption.
2. Project administrators should continuously use the platform's workflow optimization capabilities to improve the automated Delivery pipeline. This can improve Delivery efficiency and greatly reduce Credit consumption.
3. Practical experience shows that Flash models can deliver high quality for deterministic execution tasks. Use flagship models for Agents whose work determines Delivery quality, such as Clarification and code review. Flash models are recommended for other Agents, including full-stack development, deployment operations, and test case execution, to improve efficiency and reduce Credit consumption.

title: Frequently asked questions
markdown:
Q: I cannot see the detailed Delivery process in AutoWonder and feel uncertain. What should I focus on?

A: AutoWonder's AI Native SDLC changes software Delivery fundamentally compared with Vibe Coding. Agents handle the entire requirement Delivery process using the preconfigured workflow. People focus on Clarification and acceptance of the final results rather than every intermediate detail. This frees people to work on higher-value system architecture, business architecture, and business functionality, and allows one person to drive Delivery of multiple requirements in parallel.

Q: Our team wants to keep separate product, development, and testing roles. How should we configure Delivery?

A: Teams moving to full-stack development can use one Squad to deliver the whole requirement. Teams retaining traditional role-based work can design separate Squads, Agents, and SDLC workflows for their needs. Each role uses its own Squad to complete its part around the same Work item, then reaches a human decision stage. You can also specify the downstream people in the SDLC workflow; they receive an IM notification and continue Delivery using their own Squad. Once the platform's IM tool is configured, hand off to the relevant user's registered username in the SDLC workflow to send collaboration notifications. You can also manually @mention a person in Work item comments and ask them to take over the next stages.

Q: What should I do if a Work item encounters an error during Delivery?

A: @mention the relevant Agent and ask what went wrong and how to resolve it. A desktop Agent connected to AutoWonder MCP can also analyze the Work item's error. If you suspect a platform issue, connect the Agent to the AutoWonder source to investigate. If it confirms a platform defect, report the analysis to Alibaba Cloud for a fix.

Q: How many Work items can one Executor run at once, and when should I add capacity?

A: By default, each Executor for each Agent can run up to ten tasks concurrently; additional tasks queue. Because each Work item's workflow runs serially, a Squad's registered Executors can be understood as handling ten Work items at a time. If your computer or server has enough capacity, you can register multiple sets of Executors on one machine. Each task uses an isolated session, so tasks do not interfere even on the same machine. When load becomes too high, add another machine and register Executors there; the platform will schedule new tasks to it. Executors are stateless and can scale horizontally, for example by adding multiple Mac mini machines to the same project for Delivery.

Q: How should we configure project knowledge bases and development standards?

A: For business logic already expressed in code, we do not recommend maintaining a separate knowledge base or explanation: code is the best documentation. For development standards or internal terminology, use one of these approaches:
1. Maintain the documents in source repositories. Specify in the Agent definition which repository content to read and at which stage.
2. Package the development standards as a Skill, upload it to AutoWonder, and bind it to the relevant Agents. Explain in each Agent definition when to use the Skill, which knowledge to retrieve, or which standards to follow.
3. Expose your internal knowledge base as a Skill or MCP, upload it to AutoWonder, and bind it to the relevant Agents. Update the Agent instructions to integrate the enterprise knowledge base.

Q: What should I do if a Work item's workflow takes too long?

A: Consider these situations:
1. Execution time depends on the automated Delivery pipeline definition. A long workflow takes longer to complete.
2. Agent and SDLC definitions often have substantial room for improvement. Missing environment dependencies or imprecise workflow instructions can cause extra reasoning and retries, wasting time and Credits. Use an Agent to analyze and improve the definitions continuously. Also use the platform's workflow optimization capabilities to identify and improve pipeline configuration.
3. Replace model reasoning with scripts wherever scripts can accomplish the work.

AutoWonder's AI Native SDLC is a form of software Delivery for the AI era. People clarify requirements and make decisions; the automated pipeline handles the connecting and manual work that previously required people. You can focus on requirements and results instead of watching every execution step.

Focus on whether Delivery quality meets requirements, whether the automated production pipeline runs efficiently in the current environment, and whether Credit optimization meets your needs.

During working hours, people and Agents deliver requirements together. At night, Agents continue Delivery using Scheduled tasks and the automated pipeline, and you accept the results the next day. This enables 7×24-hour Delivery, with one person driving continuous Delivery of multiple requirements in parallel.

Q: What should I do if Delivery quality does not meet requirements?

A: Improve the automated pipeline for the specific problems. Use unit, integration, E2E, feature, and Playwright tests to protect quality. Add development standards and requirements to the pipeline through Skills, project documents, and similar mechanisms.

Q: What should I do if the frontend does not match the intended design closely enough?

A: Try these approaches:
1. Define frontend development standards, including element colors, spacing, and pagination styles, to improve quality.
2. Confirm the frontend design as HTML, then upload the HTML to the Work item so subsequent development can build directly from it. Design and confirmation of the HTML can be stages in the automated Delivery pipeline; arrange the workflow as needed.
